entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-62vg-58rm-qff7: @angular/router: Denial of Service via Unmatched Empty-Path Outlet Route Matching in Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
entry.content:
@angular/router: Denial of Service via Unmatched Empty-Path Outlet Route Matching in Server-Side Rendering (SSR)

Aliases: CVE-2026-111752

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • @angular/router — fixed in 22.2.1
  • @angular/router — fixed in 21.2.25
  • @angular/router — fixed in 20.3.33
  • @angular/router

A denial of service (DoS) vulnerability was identified in `@angular/router` when Server-Side Rendering (SSR) is enabled on Node.js (V8). During route recognition, `@angular/router` fails to validate whether an auxiliary outlet segment in the URL matches a route configured for that specific outlet name. Because unconfigured empty-path outlet groups (such as `a:/()`, `x:/(...)`, or `///(...)`) are not rejected during matching, the router repeatedly re-evaluates the route configuration against each arbitrary outlet segment provided in the URL. Aliases: CVE-2026-111759

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-5r4p-p66f-jhc7: Hono: `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths
entry.content:
Hono: `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths

Aliases: CVE-2026-109955, CVE-2026-111757

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • hono — fixed in 4.13.11

### Summary `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time after Hono has already decoded it for routing. A crafted request can be routed as one path and served as another, so middleware mounted on a static prefix does not run for a file under that prefix. ### Details Hono decodes the request path once before routing. `serveStatic` decoded it again before resolving the file. With a malformed percent-encoded sequence, the first decode leaves part of the path encoded, the router matches the encoded form, and the second decode resolves the real directory. The file is still resolved inside the configured root; this is not a traversal outside it. ### Impact An unauthenticated attacker may reach static files without the middleware on their prefix running, for example an authentication…

An open redirect vulnerability was identified in `@angular/platform-server` when Server-Side Rendering (SSR) is enabled. When Angular SSR renders an incoming request, URL resolution and platform navigation are managed by `ServerPlatformLocation` using `resolveUrl` (or `parseUrl` in v20). entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-8f34-f56x-9xph: msgpack5: Truncated map32 headers throw an unexpected error
entry.content:
msgpack5: Truncated map32 headers throw an unexpected error

Aliases: CVE-2026-107302

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • msgpack5 — fixed in 6.1.0

### Impact A truncated `map32` header causes an out-of-bounds buffer read and throws `RangeError` instead of `IncompleteBufferError`. Applications that rely on `IncompleteBufferError` to wait for additional bytes may terminate a request, stream, or worker unexpectedly. No adjacent memory is disclosed because the buffer implementation checks bounds. ### Patches The decoder now validates the complete five-byte `map32` header before reading its length and reports truncated input as `IncompleteBufferError`. ### Workarounds Require at least five bytes before decoding a value beginning with `0xdf`, or catch `RangeError` and treat it as incomplete input only for truncated `map32` headers.
